Smyrna
SMUR-nuh
proper noun (place)
Greek Smurna, related to smurna, "myrrh" — the bitter, fragrant resin used for embalming. A fitting name for the church of suffering, whose faithfulness was crushed like myrrh into sweetness before God.

📖 Biblical Definition

Smyrna was a wealthy port city of the Roman province of Asia, north of Ephesus, and the second of the seven churches addressed by the glorified Christ in the Revelation (Rev 2:8-11). To Smyrna alone, with Philadelphia, the Lord speaks no word of rebuke. He presents Himself as "the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive" — the very comfort a persecuted, dying church needs. He knows their works, their tribulation, and their poverty, and then adds the great reversal: "but thou art rich" (Rev 2:9). They were materially poor and slandered by "them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan." The Lord does not promise escape but forewarns of prison and "tribulation ten days," calling them to a costly fidelity: "be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life" (Rev 2:10). The overcomer "shall not be hurt of the second death." Smyrna is the pattern of the suffering church in every age — poor in this world, rich toward God, and faithful unto the scaffold. Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, would in the next century seal this very testimony with his blood.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The persecuted port-city church of Revelation 2:8-11, poor yet rich, slandered by the synagogue of Satan, called to be faithful unto death for the crown of life; one of only two churches the Lord does not rebuke.

SMYRNA, proper noun. A wealthy port city of Asia Minor; the second of the seven churches of the Revelation (Rev 2:8-11).

Addressed by Christ as "the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive."

A church of poverty and persecution — yet pronounced rich (Rev 2:9).

Slandered by the synagogue of Satan; forewarned of tribulation ten days.

Called to be faithful unto death for the crown of life; the overcomer escapes the second death.

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 2:8 — "And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive;"

Rev 2:9 — "I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan."

Rev 2:10 — "Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life."

Rev 2:11 — "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Smyrna is corrupted when its poverty-yet-riches is inverted into a prosperity gospel, or when its call to be faithful unto death is softened into a promise of earthly comfort and escape from suffering.

expand to see more

Prosperity-gospel inversion. The health-and-wealth teacher reads "but thou art rich" as a pledge of material increase, exactly reversing the Lord's meaning. Smyrna was materially poor and spiritually rich — the riches are treasure in heaven, not gold on earth. The Lord promises this faithful church not prosperity but prison, not ease but a crown won through death. To preach Smyrna as a wealth text is to preach the precise opposite of the words, flattering the flesh where Christ steeled the soul for martyrdom.

Suffering-denied misreading. Modern therapeutic religion recoils from "be thou faithful unto death" and recasts the Christian life as a path to self-actualization and emotional well-being. But the Lord of Smyrna does not spare His people tribulation; He sanctifies them through it and crowns them after it. The dictionary holds with Scripture that the church is often called to suffer, that faithfulness may cost everything, and that the crown of life is laid up for those who love not their lives unto the death (Rev 12:11).

The persecuted myrrh-named church of Revelation 2, poor yet rich, called to faithfulness unto death for the crown of life.

Usage

"Smyrna — the suffering church the Lord does not rebuke, poor in the world and rich toward God (Rev 2:9)."
